title: Enzymes
short: Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy. The substrate fits the active site; the enzyme is not used up and can work again and again.
trouble: Students think enzymes are used up in the reaction or that they supply the energy for it. Enzymes come out unchanged and only lower the energy barrier.

blocks.html: A sugar cube can sit in air for years without reacting with oxygen, yet your cells break down sugar in seconds at 37 °C. The difference is enzymes, the most important job of the proteins you just met.

Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy. The substrate fits the enzyme's active site. The enzyme is not used up: it releases the products unchanged and can work again and again.

Every reaction, even one that releases energy overall, needs a push to get started: the activation energy, the hill the molecules must climb before they can roll downhill. An enzyme gives the reaction an easier path with a lower hill. It does not change where the reaction starts or ends, so the energy released (or absorbed) overall stays the same.

blocks.name: bi-enzyme
blocks.cap: Activation energy with and without an enzyme. The start and end levels do not change.

items: The substrate binds to the active site, a pocket with just the right shape and chemistry.
The enzyme changes shape slightly to grip the substrate (induced fit), straining its bonds.
The reaction happens; the products are released.
The enzyme, unchanged, binds a new substrate. Many enzymes handle thousands of substrate molecules every second.

blocks.name: bi-enzyme
blocks.cap: Bind, react, release: the enzyme comes out the same as it went in.

blocks.html: Enzymes are specific because the active site has a shape that only certain molecules fit, like a key in a lock. Many enzyme names end in -ase and name the substrate: lactase breaks lactose, lipase breaks lipids, protease breaks proteins. An inhibitor can block an enzyme, either by sitting in the active site (competitive) or by binding elsewhere and changing its shape (noncompetitive).

blocks.title: Read the energy diagram
blocks.q: Without an enzyme, a reaction's reactants sit at 40 kJ and the peak is at 120 kJ. With the enzyme, the peak is at 70 kJ. The products sit at 10 kJ. Find each activation energy and the energy released.
steps: Energy released either way: $40 - 10 = 30$ kJ. The enzyme does not change it.
blocks.a: 80 kJ and 30 kJ; 30 kJ released in both cases

blocks.html: Thinking enzymes are used up in the reaction, or that they supply the energy for it. An enzyme comes out of each reaction exactly as it went in, which is why a tiny amount does so much work. It supplies no energy: it only lowers the energy barrier. Check on a diagram: the starting and ending levels are the same with or without the enzyme; only the peak moves.
